fact_previews: Seeed is a smart password generator created by Nathanael Maher.
Seeed does not run any server-side code except to count how many times the service has been used.
The algorithm that generates passwords is completely run on the device being used.
Seeed does not store any passwords, seeds, or master passwords.
Seeed only stores the count of how many times the website has been used.

fact_previews: Seeed does NOT save user information.
The only real weakness of using Seeed is if the person trying to hack knows the user is using Seeed.
If someone is trying to bruteforce attack a password generated with Seeed, it would take years to figure it out.
Seeed is meant to be completely free to use when released.
The Kickstarter campaign and Patreon funding are intended to cover the expenses of running Seeed.
